_confirmed_on_vehicle: 2026-09-15, ignition on, engine off, stationary, odometer 118904 km. byte_base 0 verified three ways: 2BC gave engine 24.75C and air 24.75C (cold engine sits at ambient) with gear = N; 2D0 gave ambient 24C from a different sensor; and the odometer appears twice, at 3F8 D1-D3 and 3FF D5-D7, both reading 118904. byte_base 1 gives a 138C air temperature on the same frame.

noise._: Payload bytes that free-run and must not count as a frame change. Bit N mutes byte N. Without these an ID republishes at its full cyclic rate for a whole ride and buries the real events.
noise._10C: D2-D3 is the 16-bit rpm word. It is real signal, not a counter, but at idle it dithers on every frame (1273-1351 observed at a fast cold idle), so the raw frame counts as changed every time and 10C republishes at the publish_min_ms floor for the whole ride. Measured 2026-09-15: a steady stream 210ms apart, which is publish_min_ms doing its job and still far too much. rpm keeps publishing as a decoded signal with its own deadband of 25 and min_ms of 500, so nothing is lost. D4 (clutch/kill) and D5 (side stand) stay live, so real events on this ID still surface.
noise._3FF: D2-D4 is a seconds counter. Measured on the bike incrementing by exactly 1 every 1000ms. The sheet documents it for the S1000R and its contributor could not find a use for it either. D1 (ambient light) and D5-D7 (odometer) stay live.
noise._2BC: D3-D4 is a 16-bit accumulator that only runs with the engine. Measured at idle climbing about 100 counts every 300ms, strictly monotonic, and it froze the instant the ignition went off. Purpose unknown (engine revolutions, run time or fuel used are all plausible) and it is in no published decode table. It made 2BC the noisiest ID on the bus by a wide margin: 347 raw publishes from 3857 frames, 9%, versus 1% for everything else. D2 (engine temperature) is deliberately NOT masked, so real temperature changes still publish. The current value stays visible in /can/ids and on the 60s heartbeat.
noise._2AC: CONFIRMED a rolling counter on the K25, not state. Unmasked on the vehicle 2026-09-15 during a horn test: D1 high nibble steps 0-E and wraps (low nibble static 3) and D0 steps alongside, one increment every 99ms, continuously, whatever the rider does. That matches the sheet's S1000R description closely enough to settle it. Nothing in this frame responded to any switch.

_byte_base: Dn is data[n]. The source table is the community BMW Motorrad CAN sheet, whose Key tab defines the payload as D0..D7; its 2013 ancestor numbered the same fields byte1..byte8, and the K25 Arduino sniffer built from that ancestor reads heated grips from data[7] and throttle from data[1], which is D7 and D1 here. Set to 1 only for a table written with D1 meaning data[0].
_sources: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1tUrOES5fQZa92Robr6uP8v2dzQDq9ohHjUiTU3isqdc (BMW Motorrad CAN messages, Keith Conger et al.)
https://github.com/4G-Gregg/BMW-GS-CAN-Sniffer (2010 R1200GS, Arduino; Event_Printer.ino is the ground truth for what actually ran on a K25)

outputs._: Outputs driven from decoded signals. This is the only part of the file that makes the board act rather than watch; the CAN controller stays in hardware listen-only mode regardless. An output drives local GPIOs, remote Modbus coils, or both. gpios[] forbidden on this board: 15/16 (CAN), 17/18/21 (RS485), 26-37 (SPI flash and the octal PSRAM this ESP32-S3R8 carries), 0/3/45/46 (strapping), 19/20 (USB), 43/44 (console UART). The loader rejects those with a 400 rather than taking out the flash interface.

driving._wiring: The lights are at the front and this board is under the seat, so the relays moved out to a MOSFET node at the headlight and the two of them talk Modbus RTU over one RS485 pair. Coil 0 = left lamp, coil 1 = right. The node has four channels; coils 2 and 3 are spare and the master writes them off every cycle, because it owns the slave's whole coil space (see desiredCoils() in Actions.h). Requires modbus_enable=1 in the device settings; it ships 0 so a board with no node wired to it does not spend every cycle timing out. RS485 pins are fixed by the board: TX=IO17, RX=IO18, DE=IO21, and DE is driven as the UART's RTS in half-duplex mode, per Waveshare's own WS_GPIO.h.
driving._gpio_alternative: gpios[] is empty because nothing local is wired any more. To drive relays straight off this board instead, set gpios to [4, 5]: IO4 = P1 pin 11 -> relay IN1, IO5 = P1 pin 13 -> relay IN2, P1 pin 3 or 4 = GND -> relay DC-. P1 is the internal 2x10 header, confirmed from the Waveshare schematic: 1 3V3, 2 5V, 3 GND, 4 GND, 5 TXD, 6 D_P, 7 RXD, 8 D_N, 9 IO3, 10 IO14, 11 IO4, 12 IO13, 13 IO5, 14 IO12, 15 IO6, 16 IO11, 17 IO7, 18 IO10, 19 IO8, 20 IO9. IO4-IO14 are unallocated on this board per the schematic's own GPIO table; pin 9 is IO3, a strapping pin, and the loader rejects it. FIT A 10K PULL-DOWN FROM EACH IN TO DC-: the pin floats during reset and the first moments of boot, and a floating high-trigger input can close the relay. Firmware cannot cover that window. The same warning applies to the MOSFET node's own gate pins.
driving._note: Two auxiliary driving lights, switched together. active_low applies to gpios only - a coil carries the logical state and the slave owns its polarity. auto_off_ms 0 means no timeout; set it to e.g. 3600000 for a one-hour battery backstop. off_when drops the lights when the ZFE reports the ignition off. THAT IS NOT THE FAILSAFE: if the front node is on constant power and this board is on switched, ignition-off kills the master and the node simply holds its last coil state with the lights on. The failsafe is the node's own comms watchdog - no valid write for N seconds, everything off. Keep N several times modbus_period_ms (1000ms), e.g. 5s.

gestures.name: driving_lights
gestures._note: Three clicks of the high beam turns the driving lights on, one click turns them off. A click is a COMPLETE SHORT PULSE: the signal must reach trigger and leave it again within max_hold_ms, and it is counted on release. Holding the high beam on is therefore never a click, and a hold longer than max_hold_ms cancels a sequence in progress. TIMING, measured on the bike 2026-09-15: the 130 frame only carries high beam state every 200ms, so a click costs two frames minimum and clicks cannot be closer than about 400ms. A fast flick whose press AND release fall between two frames never reaches the bus at all, which is how a deliberate three-click burst came back as two clicks and then one. Click deliberately, around half a second apart, rather than quickly. window_ms was widened from 1000 to 2500 to absorb a dropped or late pulse; it costs nothing on the triple because a burst now fires the instant it reaches the highest mapped count (3) without waiting for the window. Only the 1-click case waits, and waiting 2.5s to switch the lights off is fine. max_hold_ms 900 so a slightly lingering press still counts rather than cancelling. The consequence of 1=off is that a deliberate flash-to-pass switches the driving lights off; that was chosen knowingly. Change the '1' key to '2' if it becomes a nuisance. Any enum signal can drive this - info_button, turn_signals - by name, with no firmware change.

_extraction: bytes[] is little-endian, least-significant first: (D3*256+D2) is bytes:[2,3]. nibble is 'high' or 'low'. value = raw*scale + offset. map keys are uppercase hex of the extracted value; 'default' labels any code not in the map, otherwise it reports as unmapped_0xNN. deadband/min_ms suppress chatter on analog signals.

10C.name: engine
10C._note: asc_abs was removed here. The sheet put side stand on D5's high nibble and ASC/ABS on its low nibble; the bike proves the side stand is the LOW nibble, so the ASC signal was reading the stand and reporting off/on as the stand moved. ASC/ABS state has no confirmed home on this bus. D5's high nibble sat at E throughout and is a candidate.

signals.name: clutch_kill
signals._note: CONFIRMED on the vehicle 2026-09-15 by stopping a running engine on the kill switch. D4 went 0x16 to 0x15 at the instant rpm collapsed from 1184 to 0, a full second before the ignition went off, so it was the kill switch and not the key. The LOW nibble made that move, 6 = clutch_out to 5 = kill_switch_on, landing on the map's own values. The high nibble sat at 1 throughout and never moved. That is the sheet wrong about which nibble for the second signal in a row, and the Arduino sniffer right again. clutch_in = A is still untested: pull the lever with the engine running and watch for 6 -> A.

signals.name: side_stand
signals._note: CONFIRMED on the vehicle 2026-09-15, bike on the CENTRE stand so the side stand began up. D5 read E9 with it up, E5 while it was pulled down, E9 again once returned. So the low nibble carries it, 9 up and 5 down. The sheet is wrong twice over here: it names the HIGH nibble, which sat at E throughout and never moved, and it inverts the values as 5=Up 9=Down. Values were initially recorded inverted here too, from assuming a parked bike rests on its side stand; it did not. OPEN: a third value B appeared 2026-09-15 at the instant the engine was killed (D5 E9 -> EB), in the same frame as D4's clutch nibble going 6 -> 5, and reported as unmapped_0xB. So the low nibble is not purely the stand. 9=1001, 5=0101, B=1011 does not decompose cleanly into a stand bit plus a run bit; it is left unmapped rather than guessed. The stand result itself stands, having been produced by physically moving the stand twice.

signals.name: throttle_pct
signals._note: The current sheet says D6(High Nibble) with a /255 formula. The 2013 sheet listed this as whole byte 7 (D6) with the same formula and the K50 row uses a whole byte too; the nibble label is a later transcription slip. Whole byte used. Should track throttle_valve_pct.

signals.name: high_beam
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: LO_NIBBLE(data[6]), 9 on / A off.

signals.name: turn_signals
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: whole data[7].

signals.name: abs
signals._note: UNRESOLVED. Sheet says low nibble of D1, the Arduino sniffer reads the high nibble, same 5/B values. On the bike D1 read 0x5F: the HIGH nibble holds 5 = on, which favours the sniffer, and ABS being on with the ignition on is right. D1 is the only byte of 294 that moved. Cycle ABS off, mark it, and confirm.

signals.name: front_wheel_speed_kmh
signals._note: The ~0.06 dates from the original 2013 entry and was never firmed up. No GPS needed: at steady speed in a straight line front and rear must agree, so scale = 0.06 * rear_raw / front_raw. Adjust here once measured.

signals.name: brake_levers
signals._note: Two encodings: static values (03/07/0B/0F) and, after two full wheel revolutions, in-motion values (00/04/08/0C). Both folded into one map since the values do not collide. The Arduino sniffer reads the low nibble with 3/7/B, which is the same thing.

signals.name: engine_temp_c
signals._note: deadband must exceed one quantisation step (scale), or a sensor resting between two codes reports forever. Observed on the bike dithering 0x40/0x41 = 24.0/24.8 C, which cleared the old 0.5 deadband every time. 1.0 swallows one step and still reports two.

signals.name: gear
signals._note: The 2013 sheet said the LOW nibble; the current sheet says HIGH, attributed to eight models including the K25, and assigns the low nibble to an oil-level fault flag. High nibble used.

signals.name: air_temp_c
signals._note: Same 0.75 quantum as engine_temp_c, so the same deadband rule applies.

signals.name: ambient_air_temp_c
signals._note: 0xFF means no reading, seen for about a minute after the ignition is switched on before the ZFE has a value. Without the sentinel that publishes an ambient temperature of 87.5C, which is impossible on a motorcycle and was observed doing exactly that. Real readings sit around 0x7E-0x81.

signals.name: esa_preload
signals._note: Read C on the bike, which is 'Not Displayed' in the sheet's F800GT column, i.e. no ESA on this machine. Mapped to not_fitted rather than left unmapped. esa_damping likewise reads B,F which is outside its map.

signals.name: info_button
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: LO_NIBBLE(data[5]), 5 short / 6 long.

signals.name: heated_grips
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: HI_NIBBLE(data[7]), C/D/E. F is the whole-byte FF the ZFE sends with the ignition off, so it is labelled rather than reported as unmapped.

signals.name: ignition
signals._note: The sheet's FF=Off/DF=On row was contributed for the K25 and F800GSA and its 'DF' is simply the grips-low value with a fixed low nibble; it does not contradict heated_grips, it observed the same byte with the grips on low. Encoded as: FF means off, any other value means on.

32F.name: tyre_pressure
32F._note: RDC IS fitted on this bike, contrary to the first reading. The senders sleep when parked and report 0xFF; moving the bike woke the front one, which then read D6=0x76 = 2.36 bar (34 psi), sane for a GS against a ~2.5 bar spec. The invalid sentinel did exactly its job: silence while asleep, real value once awake. D4 and D5 woke and slept in step with D6 and D7, so the frame is very likely front/rear pairs, D4+D6 front and D5+D7 rear, with D4/D5 as tyre temperature. D4 read 0x3E = 62, which is 22C under the -40 offset TPMS senders normally use and matches ambient. NOT added as signals: the offset is a guess and a wrong one would publish fiction, which is the mistake this file has already made twice.

signals.name: rdc_rear_bar
signals._note: Both bytes read FF on this bike, i.e. no RDC senders fitted. Without the invalid sentinel that publishes a confident and fictional 5.10 bar.

signals.name: ambient_light
signals._note: Sheet: B dark, 7 light, 3 and F unknown. The Arduino sniffer used 7 dark, 3 light. Read 9 on the bike in daylight with the ignition on, so neither source is right yet. Unmapped codes surface as unmapped_0xN; record what it sends in the dark and in sunlight.

signals.name: odometer_km_alt
signals._note: Second odometer copy. Confirmed on the bike: both this and 3F8 odometer_km read 118904.

signals.name: countdown
signals._note: Source lists no formula. Raw byte, published for identification.
